oncall-bot: INCIDENT: pager fired for pg-api-rate-limit spike — primary unavailable. auto-escalation requested. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-342 :rotating_light:

Maya: sorry team — stuck at the airport, phone's low. can't hold the shift tonight. tagging for a handover. /cc @Sahil @Eli

Sahil: I can pick up primary for the next ~4h (logged on, US->EU overlap). need quick context and runbook pointer.

Eli: I can be secondary shadow for the first 2h. Will monitor metrics and logs.

Maya: quick context: spikes on /v1/generate -> tokenization -> long KV-cache warmup. Symptoms: high queue_time, per-worker token latency jumps. Customer-facing errors are 429 and increased tail p99 latency. Affected region: eu-west-1. Known mitigation: scale up model-worker-autoscaler and restart model-worker pods if stuck.

Maya: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/pg-api-rate. key steps pasted below:
```
1) Check autoscaler: kubectl -n inference get hpa model-worker-autoscaler -o yaml
2) Inspect worker logs: kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-worker -c runner --tail=200
3) If queue_time > 200ms and backlog rising, scale up by +2 nodes: runbook-scaler --scale model-worker 2
4) Soft restart: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-worker
5) If restart doesn't reduce p99 in 10m, fallback to model-variant with lower mem footprint: /api/model/variants
```

ops-bot: customer-impact: 1 paying customer showing degraded requests (acct: AcmeCorp). Auto-ticket created #INC-342-acme. PagerDuty escalation policy active.

deploy-bot: last deploy to inference cluster was 3h ago: commit ab12ef3 by @Jade. No ongoing deploys.

Nina: heads-up — if this escalates to P1 we need outreach. @Sahil please confirm you can update status page and notify SRE manager if 30m no improvement.

Sahil: taking primary. I've claimed the pager and updated rotation (using /oncall claim Sahil). Will run steps 1-3 now. @Eli please keep an eye on the customer queue.

Eli: watching logs. If you want me to restart pods I can. Requesting access to runbook-scaler (I have exec rights to kubectl but not the scaler script).

Sahil: copying commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n inference get hpa model-worker-autoscaler
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-worker -c runner --tail=200 | grep "queue_time"
/runbooks/runbook-scaler --scale model-worker 2  # dry-run then apply
```

Sahil: FYI I see worker pods OOM events at 02:14 UTC, likely memory pressure from larger batch sizes. Starting +2 scale now.

oncall-bot: rotation updated: primary=Sahil, secondary=Eli. Incident updated INC-2026-342. Pager ownership transferred.

Sahil: scaled +2, restarted deployment. Monitoring p99 and error rate. If p99 doesn't fall under 600ms in 10m we'll consider model-variant fallback. I'll post updates every 5-10m. 

Maya: thanks all — super grateful. I'll remain reachable via DM if any historical context needed. Safe handover.

Eli: saw p99 drop to 420ms after restart, errors decreased from 8% -> 1.5%. I'll keep shadow for the next 90 minutes then hand back to on-call rotation.

Sahil: marking as active mitigation. Updating status page: "Partial degradation in eu-west-1; mitigation in progress."

Nina: noted. If improvement holds after 60m, we'll close the incident and record a short postmortem. If not, escalate.

Sahil: thanks team — closing my primary shift in 3h or earlier if rotation comes up. Leaving runbook notes and commands in the incident timeline.

oncall-bot: thread closed for updates — will reopen on new events. :white_check_mark:
